title: Slide open a small stiff window by its delicate handle
instruction: The window is stiff and its handle is delicate. Grip the handle and slide the window open.
context: Robots in homes, care homes and offices will open windows, cabinet doors and hatches whose runners have stiffened, by handles that are often small plastic or glued-on fittings. Pulling hard to beat the stiffness tears such a handle off. Here the sash drags harder the faster it moves, so the robot has to open it at a pace the handle can bear.
setup: Station table with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. All sizes and positions in cm, positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the table top. Window: a small white sliding window fixed to the table, its frame and sash white uPVC (PVC-U) profile and its panes 3 mm float glass, its frame 2.8 deep (x 28.6 to 31.4), 52.4 wide (y 21.2 to -31.2) and 20.4 tall, with a 1.2 sill, head and jambs around an opening 18 tall from y 20 to -30. Right half: a fixed glazed pane (3 mm glass in a frame 1.4 wide) at the back of the frame. Left half: the sash, a glazed frame 23 wide (y 20 to -3), 18 tall and 1.2 deep at the front of the frame (x 28.7 to 29.9), 500 g, that slides right in front of the fixed pane, up to 24. It slides on the frame's uPVC track and is closed at the start. It is stiff: it drags with about 3 N for every cm/s it moves (300 N s/m). For real trials, this comes from a linear viscous damper under the sill (for example an adjustable air dashpot or a rotary oil damper driving a pinion on a rack fixed to the sash's bottom rail), set so that a steady 6 N pull on the handle, read on a spring scale, moves the sash at 2 cm/s. Handle: a chrome-plated zinc D-handle on the sash's right edge, at y -2.3: a grip bar 1 (x) x 1.2 (y) x 7 tall, 5.7 to 12.7 above the table, held 3.2 out from the sash's face (x 24.5 to 25.5) by two stand-offs. It tears off if pulled with more than about 14 N. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Only how far the sash has been pulled open by its handle counts: travel made while a gripper is closed on the handle's grip bar and pulling the sash through it. Travel made any other way, such as pushing the sash or its frame, pushing the handle without gripping it, or the sash moving after the gripper has let go, doesn't count. In real trials, read it from the trial video and a ruler: mark the sash's position each time a gripper closes on the grip bar and each time it lets go, and add up the opening made between those marks while no other part of the robot touches the sash, its glass or the frame, up to how far the sash is open at the end (from the left jamb to the sash's left edge). In the simulation: sash travel counts while a gripper's tool point is within 1 cm of the grip bar's centre (in depth and along the window), its fingers are closed on the bar (not open, not shut empty), and the handle's fixings have given at least 1 mm (0.8 N) in the opening direction. With the handle on: 1.0 at 15 cm or more pulled open (in the simulation the trial ends with 1.0 once the sash has moved under 1 cm/s for 1 s), 0.75 at 12 to 15 cm, 0.5 at 8 to 12 cm, 0.25 at 4 to 8 cm, 0 under 4 cm. Score 0 if the handle has torn off or come loose at any point (in the simulation: it gave 1.8 cm along the sash, which takes about 14 N), or if the glass or frame is damaged. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the sash closed after each trial. For real trials, check the damper before each session: a steady 6 N pull on the handle should move the sash at about 2 cm/s (300 N s/m). Use a handle that breaks away at about 14 N (for example, held on by a breakaway magnet or a calibrated shear pin) and refit or replace it after a tear.
fidelity: Approximate. The window is rigid boxes. The sash's stiffness is pure viscous damping (drag proportional to speed, no static friction), which a real dashpot reproduces closely. The handle's fixings are a spring that gives up to 1.8 cm before tearing at about 14 N; a real handle gives far less. Nothing else can bend or break, so the glass and frame rule applies only to real trials. Whether the handle pulls the sash is read from the grippers' tool points and finger openings.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached to the window by the handle and stayed there for the rest of the minute without pulling it; the sash never moved); demo: 1.0
